target_condition.evidence_quote: The gut microbiota contributes to the pathogenesis of anorexia nervosa in humans and mice

control.evidence_quote: 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females

country.evidence_quote: recruited from three specialized centres in Denmark

body_site.evidence_quote: Stools were collected according to International Human Microbiome Standards
body_site.section: Methods — Faecal sample collection and DNA extraction

days_from_first_collection.notes: Cross-sectional human cohort; no longitudinal collection timepoints reported for humans.

location.evidence_quote: recruited from three specialized centres in Denmark
location.notes: Centres: Center for Eating Disorders (Odense University Hospital), Child and Adolescent Psychiatric Unit (Aarhus University Hospital), Unit for Psychiatric Research (Aalborg University Hospital).

probing_pocket_depth.notes: Not applicable; this is a fecal microbiome study.

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months
antibiotics_exclusion_period.notes: Also applied to control exclusion criteria: antibiotics within the last 3 months.

antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.evidence_quote: antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: DNA extraction from aliquots of faecal samples was performed following IHMS SOP P7 V2
dna_extraction_kit.section: Methods — Faecal sample collection and DNA extraction
dna_extraction_kit.notes: Protocol named (IHMS SOP P7 V2) but no matching commercial kit name from the allowed enum list was specified.

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: sequenced using the Ion Proton Sequencer (Thermo Fisher)
sequencing_platform.notes: 16S rRNA sequencing of mouse recipients/donor validation was performed on an Illumina MiSeq, a separate assay from the main human shotgun metagenomics.

age.evidence_quote: 77 female AN cases and 70 age-matched female controls
age.notes: Groups described as 'age-matched' but no numeric mean/median age reported in accessible text (likely in Supplementary Table 1/2, not provided).

age_group.evidence_quote: Child and Adolescent Psychiatric Unit (Aarhus University Hospital)
age_group.notes: Recruitment across adult and adolescent psychiatric units suggests a mixed age-group cohort, but explicit classification not given.

ancestry.evidence_quote: we only included Danish Caucasian women with AN cases

ancestry_details.evidence_quote: we only included Danish Caucasian women with AN cases

sex.evidence_quote: we decided to include only women in the present study

zigosity.notes: No twin zygosity data reported; twin heritability studies are only cited as background.

age_min.notes: Overall cohort age range not given in main text; only described as 'age-matched'. Specific ages given only for the 6 FMT donors (see samples).

age_max.notes: Same as age_min; cohort-level age range not reported in provided text.

age_years.notes: Cohort mean age not stated in main text (likely in Supplementary Table 1/2, not provided). Individual donor ages given in samples.

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Applies to both AN and HC groups as an exclusion criterion; inferred that enrolled participants were not currently on antibiotics.

bmi.evidence_quote: the exclusion criteria for the age-matched healthy control women were BMI below 18.5 or above 25 kg m 21 −2
bmi.notes: Only inclusion/exclusion BMI range for HC given (18.5-25 kg/m2); exact cohort BMI values are in Supplementary Table 2 (not provided). Individual donor BMI given in samples.

dietary_restriction.notes: In-patient/out-patient meal macronutrient composition described but not as a formal 'dietary restriction' code; mouse recipients (not human participants) received a 30% energy-restricted diet.

disease.evidence_quote: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is an eating disorder with a high mortality.
disease.notes: Case-control study: AN cases vs healthy controls (HC).

disease_details.evidence_quote: the common restricting (AN-RS) type and the less prevalent binge-eating or purging (AN-BP) type
disease_details.notes: 56 AN-RS and 21 AN-BP cases per Fig. 1 legend.

disease_response_orr.notes: Not applicable; no oncology treatment response reported.

feces_phenotype.notes: Feces used for metagenomics/FMT but no specific clinical stool phenotype (e.g., diarrhea/consistency) reported.

fmt_id.notes: No explicit donor/recipient IDs given in text, only counts (3 AN donors, 3 HC donors; 8,6,6 recipient littermates per litter).

fmt_role.evidence_quote: Faecal samples from randomly selected subsets of three patients with AN ... and three HC ... were used to colonize 6-week-old female GF littermates.
fmt_role.notes: Six human donors (3 AN-RS, 3 HC) provided stool for FMT into germ-free mouse recipients.

obgyn_birth_control.evidence_quote: regular medication of any kind apart from birth control pills, and antibiotics within the last 3 months
obgyn_birth_control.notes: Only stated that birth control pills were exempted from exclusion criteria for HC; actual usage status not given.

smoker.evidence_quote: including age, BMI, smoking and multiple drug intake were corrected
smoker.notes: Smoking history used as a confounder/covariate in models, but specific smoker/non-smoker status values are not reported in provided text.

treatment.evidence_quote: Medication included selective serotonin re-uptake inhibitors, antipsychotics and benzodiazepines.
treatment.notes: These medications were used as deconfounding covariates, indicating some AN participants were on these treatments.

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: BMI of 10.3, 11.5 and 11.7 kg m −2 , respectively) and three HC
biomarker_name.notes: Only biomarker with explicit numeric value(s) directly stated in accessible text (BMI of individual faecal donors used for FMT). Group-level clinical biomarkers (glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR, CRP) are mentioned qualitatively (higher/lower) in main text but exact numeric values reside in Supplementary Table 1/2, not provided in extracted text.

biomarker_value.evidence_quote: BMI of 10.3, 11.5 and 11.7 kg m −2, respectively) and three HC (females aged 20, 22 and 21 yr with BMI of 22.6, 21.1 and 21.2 kg m −2
biomarker_value.notes: Values correspond to three AN faecal donors and three HC faecal donors used for FMT experiments, not the full 77/70 cohort.

disease_response_os.notes: No overall survival data reported; paper mentions aggregate AN mortality rate (5.6% per decade) but not individual/cohort OS durations.

ecog_performance_status.notes: Not an oncology study; ECOG performance status not applicable/reported.

feces_phenotype_value.notes: No corresponding 'feces_phenotype' categorical field defined in this schema instance to anchor a value; feces-related measures (bacterial cell counts, richness, β-diversity) are reported but not tied to a defined phenotype field.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not applicable; study concerns anorexia nervosa, not oncology.

uncurated_metadata.notes: No clearly distinct free-text metadata field beyond those already captured; omitted to avoid speculative inclusion.

host_species.evidence_quote: a cohort of 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females
host_species.notes: Primary human cohort (AN cases and healthy controls); study also used germ-free Swiss Webster mice (Mus musculus) for FMT experiments, described separately in Methods — Animal experiments.

extraction_warnings: No sample-level table with individual subject/sample IDs was present in the provided text; Supplementary Tables 1-8 were referenced but their content (numeric values, IDs) was not included, so most demographic/clinical fields (age, exact BMI, etc.) could not be extracted at the individual level.

Granularity set to subgroup_level (AN vs HC) because case-control status and some clinical characteristics are reported per group; however most descriptive fields (country, body_site, sex, ancestry, sequencing_platform) are uniform across both groups and are reported at study_level within this subgroup framework.

A small subset of 6 fecal donor samples (3 AN, 3 HC) used for mouse FMT experiments had individually reported ages and BMIs (e.g., 'females aged 20, 22 and 20 yr with BMI of 10.3, 11.5 and 11.7 kg m^-2'), but these describe donors for the mouse experiment, not the main 147-participant human cohort, and were not converted into sample-level rows to avoid conflating cohorts.
pmid and study_name were not explicitly stated in the paper text and are marked not_reported per instructions to avoid using outside knowledge (e.g., paper_id from metadata).

Full cohort (77 AN, 70 HC) demographic details (age, BMI) are reported only in Supplementary Tables 1-2, which were not included in the provided text; those study-level fields are marked not_reported.

Sample-level rows were derived only for the 6 explicitly named FMT donors (3 AN-RS, 3 HC) whose individual age and BMI were given in the Methods (Animal experiments) section; the larger human cohort and mouse recipients are only described at aggregate/subgroup level (e.g., AN-T n=10, HC-T n=10) and were not expanded into per-sample rows.
AN donor subtype was explicitly stated as AN-RS ('three randomly chosen AN-RS cases'); HC donors have no disease subtype, labeled Healthy.

antibiotics_current_use was inferred from exclusion criteria (antibiotic use within previous 3 months was an exclusion criterion for both AN and HC groups), not a directly measured/reported current-use status.
smoker field could not be assigned a specific value; smoking status is only mentioned as a covariate/confounder without categorical values reported in the main text.

biomarker_name/unit/value fields were populated with a single concrete example (donor BMI) since most clinical biomarkers (glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR, CRP) are described qualitatively in main text with exact values likely in Supplementary Tables 1-2, which were not included in the provided text.
